name: D0
summary: D0 operated at the Fermilab Tevatron, Batavia, Illinois. This historical general-purpose collider experiment tested visible dark-photon decays in hidden-valley models as portal interactions, rather than directly observing cosmic dark matter.
detection_principle: Photon, collimated-lepton-pair and large missing-transverse-energy combinations in proton–antiproton collisions test dark-photon decays in supersymmetric hidden-valley frameworks.

results.summary: No dark-photon excess above background; constraints were set on specific supersymmetric hidden-valley models.

science_scope: Tests dark-sector models by producing candidate particles or portal mediators at accelerators. Invisible accelerator final states or mediator particles alone do not establish cosmic-dark-matter identity; lifetimes, abundance and other experiments must also be considered.
